Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

internal adjective

on the inside

also inner, interior, inside (adjective), the inside of

classical

Cic. Sest. 10: in interiōre aedium parte (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 1.637: interior domus (Lewis & Short)

interior, interius

adjective, comparative in form; genitive interiōris

inner, interior

A comparative with no positive (superlative intimus, innermost): the inner part of a house, the inland peoples (Cic. Imp. Pomp. 22), the inside of anything; as a neuter plural noun, interiōra, the inside (Vulg. Jon. 1.5). The i is a vowel. A state’s internal affairs and wars are intestīnus or domesticus (Cic. Cat. 2.28; see civil, domestic).

Other words

  • internus, interna, internum — inward, internal

    also used · classical · Sen. Q.N. 6.27.2: ignis (Lewis & Short)

    (post Augustum: Ov., Sen., Tac.)

    Post-Augustan (Lewis & Short); in Tacitus mostly of a state’s own affairs and quarrels (discordiae, Ann. 2.26).

Examples

  • et Jōnās dēscendit ad interiōra nāvis, et dormiēbat sopōre gravī

    and Jonah went down into the inside of the ship and lay fast asleepVulg. Jon. 1.5

  • nōn semper ea sunt quae videntur; dēcipit frōns prīma multōs; rāra mēns intellegit quod interiōre condidit cūra angulō

    things are not always what they seem; first appearances deceive many; few minds see what care has hidden in an inner cornerPhaedr. 4.2.5–7

See also inside, outside.

SourcesLewis & Short: interior · Lewis & Short: internus · Lewis & Short: intestinus
